scenes.heading: Adding and subtracting whole numbers
scenes.sub: Fast in your head, accurate on paper
scenes.say: Totalling a shopping bill, working out change, or how far is left on a road trip: it's all adding and subtracting. Let's make you fast in your head and accurate on paper.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Swap ten $1 coins for a $10 note, or break a $10 note into ten $1 coins
scenes.science: Carrying and borrowing swap 10 ones for 1 ten, and back
scenes.breaks: Real money has $2, $5, $20 and $50 too. Place value only ever swaps in groups of exactly ten.
scenes.say: Think about money. Ten one-dollar coins can be swapped for a ten-dollar note. That's carrying. If you need to pay seven dollars but only have a ten, you break it into ten one-dollar coins. That's borrowing. Nothing is lost, you just swap. But place value only ever swaps in groups of exactly ten.

scenes.heading: Mental strategies
scenes.say: Some quick mental strategies. Jump: forty-seven plus thirty is seventy-seven, plus eight is eighty-five. Make a ten: one hundred and ninety-six plus four is two hundred. Compensate: eighty-three take thirty is fifty-three, then add back one, fifty-four. Count up: from seven hundred and sixty to one thousand is two hundred and forty.
scenes.caption: Jump: 47 + 30 = 77, + 8 = 85. Make a ten: 196 + 4 = 200. Compensate: 83 − 30 = 53, add back 1: 54. Count up: from 760 to 1000 is 240.

scenes.heading: Jump along a number line
scenes.say: Here is the jump strategy. Start at forty-seven, jump thirty to seventy-seven, then jump eight to eighty-five.
scenes.caption: 47 + 38: jump +30, then +8 → 85

scenes.heading: Count up to subtract
scenes.say: For one thousand take away seven hundred and sixty, count up: forty to eight hundred, then two hundred to one thousand. That's two hundred and forty.
scenes.caption: 1000 − 760: count up 40 + 200 = 240

scenes.heading: Column addition
scenes.question: Work out 2586 + 1347.
scenes.say: Line up the columns and start on the right. Six plus seven is thirteen: write three, carry one. Eight plus four plus one is thirteen: write three, carry one. Five plus three plus one is nine. Two plus one is three. The answer is three thousand, nine hundred and thirty-three.
scenes.caption: Line up the columns and start on the right. 6 + 7 = 13: write 3, carry 1. 8 + 4 + 1 = 13: write 3, carry 1. 5 + 3 + 1 = 9. 2 + 1 = 3. The answer is 3933.

scenes.heading: Borrowing across zeros
scenes.question: Work out 5003 − 1768.
scenes.say: Five thousand and three take one thousand, seven hundred and sixty-eight. Three is less than eight, so borrow. The zeros pass it along: the five becomes four, each zero becomes nine, and the three becomes thirteen. Now subtract each column to get three thousand, two hundred and thirty-five. Check by adding back.
scenes.caption: 5003 − 1768. 3 is less than 8, so borrow. The zeros pass it along: 5 becomes 4, each 0 becomes 9, and 3 becomes 13. Subtract each column: 3235. Check by adding back.

scenes.heading: Adding vs subtracting
scenes.say: Adding can be done in any order, and when a column reaches ten you carry. Subtracting must be done in the order written. Never flip a column to take the smaller digit from the larger. If the top digit is too small, borrow.

points: Borrow when the top digit is smaller
Estimate first, check with the inverse
scenes.say: Quick recap. Line up ones under ones and start on the right. Carry when a column reaches ten. Borrow when the top digit is smaller. Estimate first, then check by doing the opposite operation. Now try the practice questions!
